items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, Exploration design session); Claude (written into EXPLORATION.md)
items.title: Wire the Exploration tree into the sim, and validate its sizing
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: "Globalisation and industry use different trees." The chain is Colonisation -> Empire -> EXPLORATION -> Industry.

=== THE TREE IS AUTHORED (2026-09-11, resolving NR-843). WHAT REMAINS IS WIRING. ===
EXPLORATION_TREE.md and exploration_tree.json exist: 31 nodes of a 64 cap, 3 rings, 4 branches + spire (Purse / Hulls / Port & Garrison / Ways / Goods), 3 milestones, 3 forks. tree_lint.js knows the tree and passes on all four. EMPIRE_TREE.md and empire_tree.json re-point the rim milestone at it; INDUSTRY_TREE.md is gated behind its rim.

THE WORK IS THE SIM SIDE, and BL-912 (empire tree wired) is the exact precedent to copy. Add per-polity state alongside `empire_mask`: `exploration_mask` (uint64), `exploration_investing` (int16), `exploration_progress_q` (int32). Generate the node table the way gen_empire_tree_table.js does -- generalise that tool rather than forking it. Honour `excludes`: a closed fork side never sets its bit, per empire_node_available.

FOUR NEW SCORER TERMS the Empire tree cannot express, defined in EXPLORATION_TREE.md sec The scorer: `purse_low`, `wants_unmet`, `throughput_bound`, `subject_held`. THREE OF THE FOUR READ QUANTITIES THAT DO NOT EXIST YET -- the treasury (BL-932), the scarcity signal (BL-939) and corridor throughput (BL-940) -- so this item either lands after them or lands with the terms stubbed and a harness pinning each one as its quantity arrives. `throughput_bound` is the load-bearing one: it is the only term a landlocked realm with no subjects can ever be bound by, and without it the scorer has nothing to say to a consolidator.

SIZING IS AN ASSERTION, NOT A NUMBER (NR-844, TREES.md sec Sizes). 31 nodes is UNDER the ~34 target and is reported rather than padded. What the sweep must show: the leading polity reaches *The Long Reckoning* shortly before 1660, the median stands near *The Standing Charter*. If it does not, the tree wants a fourth ring -- that is a measurement, not a guess.

ONE OPEN SHAPE QUESTION worth settling while wiring: only the *Ocean Carrack* side of the Hulls fork leads to ring 3, so a realm that bought *Fleet of the Line* ends the branch. That is deliberate and it is the tree's most arguable claim; the alternative is a second ring-3 node behind the fighting fork.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, Exploration design session); Claude (written into EXPLORATION.md)
items.title: The Exploration span runs: 1200 to 1660, on the shared engine, with an upkeep step
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: "Let's use the same engine - if needs be we can revise this later."

THE SPAN. 1200 -> 1660 CE, 460 years, opening the instant the Empire pass closes. The 1200 -> 1560 coast is RETIRED (GENERATION_STRATEGY.md sec Pass 2 now records the supersession). Pass 1's 3600 years and the 1960 epoch are both unmoved.

THE ENGINE. history_sim over the same region and polity tables, taking pass_one_output as its input and nothing else. Two honest additions, both named in EXPLORATION.md sec The engine is shared: a ROUND-LEVEL UPKEEP STEP (earn, pay stocks, invest) because every other item depends on a recurring bill, and OBJECTS WITH A TERM, because treaties expire and nothing in the Empire phase does.

THE VERBS. Settle, Invest, Consolidate and Campaign carry over unchanged; what the phase adds is what a treasury makes purchasable, scored on the one shape (TREES.md sec The scorer).

NOT IN SCOPE: a second simulator, and any change to the Empire span's rules.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, Exploration design session); Claude (written into EXPLORATION.md)
items.title: The treasury: material becomes capital, and it stands at the capital seat
items.design:
=== SUPERSEDES THE 2026-09-11 MORNING RULING. Ben chose a free-floating per-polity scalar, then moved it: "The treasury is moved to the capital for this phase." ===

THE TREASURY SITS AT THE CAPITAL SEAT, one per polity, AND IT IS CAPTURABLE. That is the whole reason the location matters: CIVILISATION.md sec Materials are spent when something happens puts Empire-phase stores at the seat precisely so "a conqueror who takes the seat takes the stores standing in it", and a treasury with no location would discard that in the phase where distant conquest is supposed to pay. A fleet that sacks a capital must take something real.

CONSOLIDATION IS THE PHASE'S OPENING ACT AND IT IS VISIBLE. Ben, 2026-09-11: "We can just consolidate all stores of material into the polity level as the initial part of Exploration... it doesn't bother me if we introduce major centralisation as an initial step." At 1200 CE every seat's stores flow to the capital, ONCE. The time-lapse can show it, and it is the moment a realm stops being a set of provisioned cities and becomes a state with a purse.

FED BY four sources, all of them things the polity already holds or reaches: endowment on held ground, the inherited `surviving_corridors` network, the markets standing on its seats (`region::has_market`), and subject tribute. NOTHING TOPS IT UP -- a polity that inherited little is poor, which is the asymmetry the 1200 CE handoff exists to produce.

THIS IS WHERE CIVILISATION.md's DEFERRAL LANDS: that doc says resources become capital in pass 2 and not in the Empire phase. Exploration is pass 2's first half, so the promise is kept exactly here and the Empire span stays priceless.

OPEN, AND A MEASUREMENT NOT A GUESS: the arithmetic of the four income terms. Set it from a sweep that produces both rich and poor survivors, never from a number picked to make one seed solvent.

DONE WHEN: a capital holds a treasury, sacking a capital transfers it, the consolidation fires once at 1200, and the treasury spread across a sweep correlates with the inherited corridor network rather than with polity size alone (BL-937's reading).

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, Exploration design session); Claude (written into EXPLORATION.md)
items.title: Treaties: a bound pair with an end date, and five clause kinds
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: "We should move away from the rapid claim and grudge system. We should be creating lengthy treaties and pushing slowly towards gaining territory."

THIS OVERTURNS CIVILISATION.md's THIRD EXCLUSION, FORWARD ONLY. That doc's sec Fear of being next declines treaties, negotiation and alliance objects - correctly, for Empires, and nothing here relaxes it backwards. Exploration has real treaty objects; Empires still does not.

THE SHAPE. Same family as grudge and contact - a named pair plus what joined them - with two additions: it EXPIRES (a term of years) and it BINDS rather than records.

FIVE CLAUSE KINDS, all five settled by Ben 2026-09-11: non-aggression for a term; trade access to a market; a sphere of claim over unclaimed ground; tribute from subject to overlord; mutual defence.

NOBODY NEGOTIATES. A treaty forms when both parties independently score the binding as worth more than the freedom it costs, against the same seeded state - which keeps determinism and keeps a bargaining layer out.

BREAKING ONE IS LEGAL AND COSTLY. Defection writes into the EXISTING grudge table, and the cost lands on every other party's willingness to bind with the defector. Nothing reads the defector's own ledger to pick a target - that is revenge and stays declined.

OPEN: where the formation threshold sits. Too low and the map freezes; too high and the conflict displacement never happens. Same discipline as the opposition bar.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, Exploration design session); Claude (written into EXPLORATION.md)
items.title: A colony is a live polity with an overlord link, and it wants things of its own
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-11, elicitation): a colony is a LIVE POLITY WITH AN OVERLORD LINK - not a region annotation, not a new actor class. And (Ben, same day) colonies are "subject with their own desires."

polity::parent IS NOT THAT FIELD. parent records lineage - who this polity broke away from. Subjection is a LIVE relation that begins, ends and transfers; overloading lineage onto it makes a colony indistinguishable from a secession the moment either changes. The overlord link is its own field.

OWN DESIRES IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF. A colony keeps its own rows in the want table, pointed at what ITS ground lacks and its neighbours hold. Two consequences, both wanted: a colony can want what its overlord does not, and a colony's wants can point at a rival's colony across a frontier the metropoles have treatied over.

WHERE SUBJECTS COME FROM. There is NO TERRA NULLIUS: CIVILISATION.md sec Contact is polity to polity fixes that a far continent at 1200 CE is settled and unmet. So either a TRADE PROVINCE (a seat with a market and an overlord on a native polity's coast, the native polity surviving beside it) or a SUBJECTED POLITY (the native polity itself, brought under the link, whole). Ben, 2026-09-11: "the most technologically dominant nations are able to lay claim to polities they have no direct control over - beginning to sprout trade provinces, and steal land from natives."

THE ASYMMETRY IS A NODE, NEVER A RANK. Nothing reads size; what decides who can arrive is what the arriving polity holds.

REFUSAL IS SECESSION. Tribute is a treaty clause and a clause comes up for renewal; a subject refusing renewal should read the same quantities the Empire phase's secession reads, so a colonial empire outrunning its network fails the same way a land empire does.

OPEN: whether a colony may itself hold a colony - the link permits a chain, and the answer decides whether a subject is an actor or a leaf.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, Exploration design session); Claude (written into EXPLORATION.md)
items.title: Ports, navies and standing armies: built from capital, and they decay
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: "Spending capital on ports within the Exploration round enables cheaper overseas skirmishes. So building a navy and standing army that persists is important - these degrade over time if insufficient capital is provided."

CARRY RULE, settled by Ben 2026-09-11 (elicitation): army_stock CARRIES across the 1200 handoff; the NAVY IS NEW AND STARTS AT ZERO everywhere. So the first ocean-capable power in a world built its fleet inside this phase, and the sweep can see when.

THREE STOCKS, each maintained by the treasury. PORT: built on a region with a port window, lowers the cost of every crossing staged from it, silts toward nothing when underfunded. NAVY: staged from a port, gives crossing capacity and contest of a crossing, decays - a fleet is a running cost, not a purchase. STANDING ARMY: on top of inherited army_stock, force already raised when a skirmish opens; falls back toward what muster alone provides.

port_q IS ENDOWMENT, NOT A PORT. The region field says the ground could take a harbour. Building one is an act of this phase and is paid for; conflating the two gives every coastal polity the thing the phase is about acquiring.

WHY IT MATTERS TO THE PHASE'S CLAIM. A neighbour war is fought where treaties bind and no port discount applies; a frontier skirmish is staged from a port the polity paid for. That price gap IS the displacement of conflict, and it is a cost in the world rather than a handicap in the scorer.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, Exploration design session); Claude (written into EXPLORATION.md)
items.title: A good is wanted differently by different peoples, and the difference is traceable to route
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: Exploration "gives us cultural preference to goods, markets that trade named goods in a simplified form."

PREFERENCE ATTACHES TO A CULTURE, NOT A POLITY. Cultures already cross borders as shares on every region, so a preference carried by culture spreads with people and survives conquest - which makes a market's demand a fact about who LIVES there rather than who RULES there.

DERIVED, NEVER ROLLED (the standing rule: consequences, not dice). It follows from what the culture's ground never held and what its route exposed it to - the same two inputs derive_wants already uses, read at culture grain instead of polity grain. A people that walked past a good and never held it pays most for it.

IT WEIGHTS A WANT, IT DOES NOT SET A PRICE. The want table is directed and unpriced; preference makes some directed wants stronger, which is enough to rank where a fleet goes first. Turning a weight into a price is Digitisation's.

OPEN: how preference interacts with assimilation - whether an absorbed culture's preferences blend, persist or lapse is unowned.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, Exploration design session); Claude (written into EXPLORATION.md)
items.title: Instrument the ten Exploration readings, taken at 1660 over a seed spread
items.design:
EXPLORATION.md sec What the phase is judged on names TEN readings, all taken at 1660 CE and all over a SEED SPREAD, never per world.

=== LAND THIS FIRST, BEFORE ANY MECHANISM. Not last. ===
BL-905/BL-906 showed the Empire span's instrumentation was the thing that turned a guessed constant into a measured one, and the sprint's named risk -- the frozen map -- is INVISIBLE without it. A phase that damps conflict everywhere looks identical to a phase that displaces it until somebody measures the ratio.

THE FIRST TWO ARE ONE TEST AND MUST BE READ TOGETHER.
1. DISPLACEMENT, A RATIO (Ben, 2026-09-11): neighbour-war rate falls RELATIVE TO frontier-skirmish rate. A FALL IN BOTH IS A FAILURE, not a success. This replaced an earlier one-way reading that a world which simply stopped fighting would have passed.
2. CONFLICT PERSISTS: total conflict at 1660 below Empires' but not near zero. CIVILISATION.md's handoff requires FRAGMENTATION, not peace.

THE OTHER EIGHT. Both strategies pay: consolidators and expansionists both among the strongest realms, each traceable to its creed (BL-942). Treaty depth: standing at 1660 with years still to run, not a churn of one-round bindings. Colonial asymmetry: some hold subjects, most hold none, at least one subject under a distant overlord. Subject friction: at least one subject's wants point where its overlord's do not. Fleets: navies exist unevenly, and at least one realm built one and let it decay. Treasury spread: wide, correlated with the inherited corridor network rather than size. Throughput: corridors carrying materially different volumes with the road ladder visible in the difference. Preference: goods wanted differently by different cultures, traceable to route.

A READING IS A REQUIREMENT, NOT A TARGET. A seed that refuses one is a legitimate world; a SPREAD that refuses one is a phase that did not do its job. No number is set ahead of the measured spread.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, "we should shrink the industry tree"); Claude (found the cause while building the Exploration tree)
items.title: Industry's ring 1 is the exploration age: migrate it out and shift every ring down
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: "we should shrink the industry tree" (resolving NR-844, which reported it oversized after the span fell 400 -> 300 years).

THE NAIVE SHRINK IS WRONG AND MUST NOT BE DONE. Dropping the outer ring is the obvious cut and it removes RING 4: Electrification, Internal Combustion & Oil, Flight, Automotive Transport, Broadcast, Antibiotics & Mass Vaccination, Synthetic Chemistry, Fixed-Nitrogen Synthesis, Tractor & Fertiliser. That is the twentieth century, and the campaign epoch is 1960. Ring 4 stays.

THE REAL FINDING: RING 1 IS THE EXPLORATION AGE. Measured 2026-09-11 while authoring EXPLORATION_TREE.md. Ring 1 holds Full-Rigged Ship, Celestial Navigation, Chronometer, Joint-Stock & Public Credit, Chartered Capital, Movable-Type Press, Crop-Package Exchange. Those are 1200-1660 subjects, and they sat in the Industry tree only because no Exploration tree existed to hold them. TWO ARE OUTRIGHT DUPLICATES of nodes now authored: IN-MV-1b Full-Rigged Ship and IN-MV-1c Celestial Navigation against EX-HL-2a Ocean Carrack and EX-HL-3a Oceanic Navigation; IN-CH-1b/IN-CH-1d against EX-SP-2a The Chartered Company.

THE WORK. Ring 1 (18 nodes) migrates out: some subjects are already covered by the Exploration tree and are simply dropped, others may earn a place in it. Rings 2/3/4 shift down to 1/2/3. Industry becomes 3 rings, 5 branches, 3 milestones, ~44 nodes -- which is also the proportional target (62 x 300/400 = 46), reached by MEANING rather than by arithmetic, which is why it is believable.

EVERY NODE ID CHANGES, because an id carries its ring. That is the bulk of the work and it is mechanical: renumber, rewrite links/requires/excludes, rewrite the doc's tables, re-run tree_lint.js industry. THE RIM MILESTONE'S MEANING IS UNCHANGED -- it still opens nothing and ends the chain; only its id moves.

WATCH FOR: rule 4 breakage. Each milestone requires majors at ITS OWN ring from two branches; after a shift the old ring-2 milestone's requires are still ring-2 ids that are now ring 1, so they travel together, but any milestone whose requires named a ring-1 major that got DROPPED needs a new requirement. The lint catches this; do not hand-wave it.

DONE WHEN: tree_lint.js passes on both industry and exploration, no subject appears in both trees, ring 4's contents survive as ring 3, and TREES.md's size row states the new shape.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, Exploration design session); Claude (written into EXPLORATION.md)
items.title: A scarcity signal per good per market — the demand half, and never a price
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-11): "For prices, I like this cheap resolution of a scarcity signal."

THE PROBLEM IT RESOLVES. Ben's earlier ruling gave this phase "markets that trade named goods in a simplified form" and gave Digitisation the companies; he then said Digitisation receives "what prices different goods have." Those could not both hold. The signal is the resolution: Exploration says WHAT IS WANTED AND HOW MUCH, Digitisation resolves that into a price.

THE SHAPE. One integer per (good, market) -- how badly this market wants this good. NO CLEARING, NO ORDER BOOK, NO FIRM, NO PRICE BAND. It sits on the market regions BL-910 already stands up (`region::has_market` on capital seats).

THIS IS WHAT KEEPS CIVILISATION.md's BOUNDARY FROM DRIFTING. That doc's markets at the close are "a place and a visible condition, not an order book"; a real price in this phase would build the economy layer two phases early. The signal is the smallest thing that carries the information forward without becoming a market.

IT IS THE DEMAND HALF ONLY. BL-940 owns the flow half, and neither is sufficient alone: a want with no throughput is an appetite that never resolves, throughput with no want is traffic with no reason.

DERIVED, NEVER ROLLED. Inputs are already recorded: the directed want table (`derive_wants`), what the market's own ground is dominant in, and the holding polity's population. The existing `want::via_market` flag is the seed of this -- it already asks whether a holder's market SHOWS a good.

DONE WHEN: every market carries a signal per good, the signal is legible across the contact graph to a polity that has met it, EXPLORATION tree node EX-GD-2a (Quayside Market) makes it legible to strangers, and BL-937's preference reading can be taken off it.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, Exploration design session); Claude (written into EXPLORATION.md)
items.title: Goods move as one number per corridor, and the road ladder gets its third rung
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-11), AND A READING CORRECTED IN THE SAME EXCHANGE. Ben: "For moving goods, we should skip this as you suggested above and use scarcity signals. Let me know if I'm reading this wrong." HE WAS, BY ONE STEP. What is skipped is PER-GOOD ROUTING; what is kept is ONE NUMBER PER CORRIDOR. Skipping flow entirely would leave the fleet/caravan visual (BL-943) with no quantity to threshold against, and "throughput based logistics" with nothing to be a throughput OF.

NO CARGO OBJECT EVER EXISTS. Nothing paths a good, nothing owns a good, no convoy is an entity. GENERATION_STRATEGY.md records that the Empire pass already pays a full Dijkstra per polity per round against a region count that GROWS INSIDE THE RUN; routing goods on top of that multiplies the known hot spot across another 460 years. That is the cost this item exists to avoid.

WHAT MOVES IS A QUANTITY ON A GRAPH ALREADY WALKED. `region::network_supply_q` is already 0-1000, terrain-weighted reach from the capital over held ground, discounted by a road (BL-837) and relayed by a town (BL-887) -- throughput in everything but name. Read it along the `surviving_corridors` graph the pass already carries.

THE THIRD RUNG OF THE ROAD LADDER (Ben, 2026-09-11: "upgrade of roads"). The Empire sim promotes a corridor by USE -- Track at `road_tier1_uses` (4), Road above it, nothing beyond. This phase adds the rung above, and it is BOUGHT WITH CAPITAL rather than earned by traffic (tree node EX-WY-1a Post Roads). That is what makes a treasury matter to a realm that never sails, and it is half of the consolidator's path.

PAIRS WITH BL-939. Scarcity says what is wanted; throughput says how much arrives. The pair is what makes a trade route a consequence rather than a drawing.

DONE WHEN: corridors carry materially different volumes across a sweep, the difference is traceable to the road rung, the sim's per-round cost has not materially regressed (measure it), and `throughput_bound` (BL-930's scorer term) can read a real quantity.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, Exploration design session); Claude (written into EXPLORATION.md)
items.title: Visible force buys quiet at home and opportunity abroad — Ceiling and Alarm at polity grain
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: "military arms races which serve to reinforce peace near to home, and conflict far from home."

THE PROJECT ALREADY HAS THE SHAPE, AND IT IS NOT A NEW OBJECT. ../economy/ERAS.md sec The two scalars carries a per-nation CEILING (restraint carried) against a per-nation ALARM (how threatened this nation feels by others' VISIBLE capability), with the explicit discipline that neither is a new world entity -- the same discipline BL-223 set for the deterrence ceiling. Reuse that pair at POLITY grain; do not invent a third quantity.

VISIBILITY IS THE WHOLE MECHANISM. A standing army and a fleet are read by neighbours whether or not they are used (tree node EX-PT-2a Standing Garrison is the first thing in the Exploration tree that is visible at rest). A neighbour that reads them BINDS A TREATY (BL-933) rather than testing them. The same fleet pointed at ground whose holder has none meets no deterrent at all. ONE PURCHASE, TWO OPPOSITE EFFECTS -- that is the displacement, priced in the only currency the phase has.

IT IS A FORCE IN THE WORLD, NOT A TERM IN THE ACTOR. The standing rule against agent handicaps binds: nothing reads a scorer's own disposition to become peaceful. The scorer is untouched; what changed is that a neighbour war got expensive and a distant one did not.

THE FAILURE MODE THIS ITEM OWNS. Deterrence that works everywhere produces a FROZEN MAP, which fails CIVILISATION.md's fragmentation handoff as surely as a hegemon does. BL-937's displacement RATIO is the check, and this item is not done until that reading moves in the right direction with total conflict still well above zero.

OPEN: where the thresholds sit -- what makes a neighbour bind rather than test. Unmeasured, and a measurement rather than a judgement.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, Exploration design session); Claude (written into EXPLORATION.md)
items.title: Consolidation and expansion both pay, and a creed decides which a realm reaches for
items.design:
THE PROBLEM, NAMED BY ITS AUTHOR (Ben, 2026-09-11): "so much of this is my euro-centric view as an author, I want to consider how we can also strengthen larger empires which do not have an interest in colonization / spreading faith."

THE RISK IS IN THE SCOREBOARD, NOT THE MECHANICS. If the phase's readings only measure colonies and fleets, a continental realm has no way to succeed at it, every world converges on one strategy, and the flat map GENERATION_STRATEGY.md sec Asymmetry is the deliverable exists to prevent is exactly what generation produces.

TWO STRATEGIES, BOTH PAYING. EXPANSION buys ports, hulls, subjects and trade provinces; wants goods it lacks from strangers; grows outward; fails by outrunning its network. CONSOLIDATION buys the road ladder, dense internal throughput and its own ground worked harder; wants reach and yield it already owns; grows inward; fails by stagnating. EXPLORATION.md sec Two ways to be strong carries the table.

NEITHER IS A FLAG AND NEITHER IS CHOSEN (Ben, 2026-09-11): "Ideally we can let candidates work on either consolidation or expansion depending on their historical creed."

THE MATERIAL IS ALREADY RECORDED AND NOTHING NEW NEEDS INVENTING. A pantheon's gods carry `zeal` (relishes battle) and `dominion` (expects to prevail), 0-10 (`culture_god`, creeds.hpp); `sea_legs_q` is earned from a coastal cradle, a migration crossing, and a sea or storm god. HIGH DOMINION WITH NO SEA LEGS IS THE CONTINENTAL CONSOLIDATOR, already derivable. Deep sea legs with a universalising creed is the coloniser.

THE SCORER TERM THAT MAKES IT LEGIBLE is `throughput_bound` (BL-930, BL-940) -- the only pressure a realm with no coast and no subjects can ever be under. Without it the scorer has nothing to say to a consolidator and this item is decoration.

IF THE MAPPING DOES NOT SEPARATE THEM, THE FIX IS UPSTREAM (Ben, 2026-09-11: "if we have to force this outcome, then we should be looking back at the Empire phase to ensure creeds map well to our phase"). Forcing a disposition the creeds do not support would be a term inside an actor and stays declined.

DONE WHEN: BL-937's "both strategies pay" reading is green across a sweep -- consolidators and expansionists both among the strongest realms, each traceable to its creed's recorded deeds.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, Exploration design session); Claude (written into EXPLORATION.md)
items.title: Draw a fleet or a caravan when a corridor's throughput crosses a threshold
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: "We also want to visualise fleets and caravans moving, this can be heavily abstracted since the pace of our time-lapse is too fast, so we will just render examples when a threshold supply is reached."

AN EXEMPLAR STANDS FOR THE FLOW; IT DOES NOT DEPICT IT. One sail, one caravan, drawn on a corridor whose throughput crosses a threshold. Not one mark per cargo, not an animation of traffic -- the time-lapse runs centuries per second and a faithful depiction would be noise.

THIS COSTS A COMPARISON, AND ONLY BECAUSE BL-940 EXISTS. The flow is already one number per corridor, so the visual is a FILTER ON THAT NUMBER rather than a second simulation. If this item is reached before BL-940, it has nothing to read -- that dependency is the whole reason the corridor number was kept when per-good routing was cut.

WHERE IT DRAWS. The Exploration span's round in the wizard, beside the existing era time-lapse surface (BL-916's typed event layer, BL-919's lineage palette, BL-915's terrain underlay). Sea exemplars on water corridors, land exemplars on road corridors, and the ROAD RUNG should be legible in the mark -- a Highway corridor and a Track corridor must not draw the same.

ALSO DRAW THE CONSOLIDATION (BL-932). The one-time flow of seat stores into the capital at 1200 is the phase's opening act and Ben called it out as something the lapse can show.

A VISUAL REQUIREMENT NEEDS A LIVE CLICK, not only a capture (standing rules). Arrive on the Exploration round in the built app and watch it.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, Exploration design session); Claude (written into EXPLORATION.md)
items.title: Faith fractures an empire — the schism verb, and the reassertion that never fires
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-11: "faith is another strong lever for conflict in this phase - we could even model a schism." THE REFERENCE IS A MECHANISM AND THE NAME IS NEVER CONTENT (standing rule): the creed is generated and named by the phoneme banks like every other.

THE SUBSTRATE IS BUILT AND WAS LEFT DELIBERATELY OPEN. The universalising creed landed 2026-09-11: a `universal_creed` record belonging to nobody, `polity::universal_creed` as the INSTITUTION, `region::creed_hold` (none / dual-hold / converted / reasserted) as the PEOPLE, and `region::creed_residue_culture` recorded at contact and kept whichever way the pair resolves -- which is precisely the line a schism cuts along. CREEDS.md sec The four calls, settled owns it. The schism VERB was named as a later slice; this is that slice.

=== READ THIS BEFORE BUILDING: REASSERTION FIRED ZERO TIMES IN 16 WORLDS. ===
Measured on delivery. The branch is live and correct but unexercised: held ground under an adopting realm sits well above the binding floor, because BL-896's secession floor has ALREADY removed the badly-reached ground. So the TURMOIL half of the creed design currently does nothing, and A SCHISM BUILT ON TOP OF IT WOULD ALSO FIRE ZERO TIMES. `universal_creed_convert_supply_q` and `universal_creed_alien_penalty_q` are the dials; the honest reading recorded on delivery is that it needs a higher floor or a SECOND BINDING TERM. THAT IS BEN'S CALL AND IT GATES THIS ITEM -- fix the substrate first, or this builds a verb nothing reaches.

WHY THE PHASE WANTS IT. CREEDS.md already argues a universalising creed gives a motive to expand toward PEOPLE rather than toward GROUND, and gives a SECOND, INDEPENDENT WAY TO FALL -- one that has nothing to do with distance. Exploration needs exactly that: a source of conflict that is not the arms race and not a want, and one a NON-COLONISING realm can be torn apart by (BL-942).

THE FAULT LINE IS ALREADY NAMED: the gap between a polity's adopted institution and its peoples' uneven conversion. An empire whose institution is universal and whose subject peoples are not is exactly the empire that splits over faith rather than over distance.

DONE WHEN: reassertion fires in some worlds and not others as a consequence of upstream scalars; a schism fractures at least one realm in a sweep along the residue line; and the fracture is distinguishable in the readings from a network-failure collapse.

items.title: Spend is estimated once at 1960 and seeds the campaign's depletion reserve
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-11): "For depletion accounting, I would prefer if we retrofit this, and come to a sensible estimate at the very end of digitisation. For generation you are right in that keeping items abstract is best policy." So NO ACCUMULATOR IS ADDED anywhere in the history sim, and sprint 39's closed Empire span is NOT reopened.

WHY IT MATTERS. Ben, 2026-09-11, on what digitisation passes forward: "the main levers we pass are going to be about how much of easily accessible resource has been actually spent." The saturated corporate web forms around what is LEFT.

WHERE IT LANDS IS ALREADY BUILT, AND THIS IS THE ELEGANT PART. `tile_component::resource_remaining` (components.hpp) is a finite reserve, live, drawn down by extraction and tapering output as it empties -- and it is SEEDED AT GENERATION to richness x a reserve factor (tile_generation.cpp). The two economy phases set that seed instead of a constant. Ground worked for centuries hands the campaign a thinner reserve. No new field, no new accumulator, no change to the campaign's extraction loop.

THE PRICE OF RETROFITTING, STATED PLAINLY AND ACCEPTED. An estimate computed once at 1960 can NEVER BE CHECKED against what actually happened, because nothing recorded it. That makes it a STATED FORMULA rather than a measurement. THE FORMULA MUST THEREFORE BE WRITTEN DOWN AS ONE -- named inputs, named arithmetic, in DIGITISATION.md -- or it silently becomes a fudge factor nobody can audit. Writing it down IS the work; an unwritten estimate is the failure mode.

ITS INPUTS ARE THE ABSTRACT ONES THE SIM ALREADY HOLDS: how long ground was held and worked, its `dominant` region class, whether it industrialised and when, and the corridor throughput that ran off it (BL-940).

PARKED UNTIL DIGITISATION IS DESIGNED. DIGITISATION.md is a placeholder by Ben's ruling; this item is filed now so the decision is not lost, and it is NOT sprint 40 work.
